title.narrative: Protecting Civilians Enabling Humanitarian Partners to Deliver Aid/Services Free from Risk of EO in Prioritised Locations in Aleppo Damascus.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to remove the threat of explosive ordnance (EO) for communities most at risk through the implementation of humanitarian mine action activities in line with the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP). ltbrgtUNMAS aims to ensure that the people residing in the identified areas are protected from EO risks and able to safely access aid and basic services, and that humanitarian and early recovery actors are able to deliver free from the risk of EO contamination. This will further enable the communities to safely utilize cleared land for productive use, supporting local agricultural and livelihood opportunities, enhancing community resilience and reducing reliance on aid. ltbrgtMore specifically, in accordance with the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF) 2024 Standard Allocation’ priorities1 2, this project envisions to reduce the impact of explosive ordnance through survey, clearance and explosive ordinance risk education (EORE) activities in several priority locations in Rural Damascus and Aleppo. Survey is essential to define the scale and scope of explosive ordnance contamination and identify the appropriate measures to mitigate the threat. Clearance is the only way to permanently remove existing explosive threats. Risk Education is the first step towards raising awareness about EO threats. Together, these activities are critical enablers for communities to mitigate the EO risks (e.g. recognize explosive ordnance threats and adopt safe behaviors) and to gain access to basic services and livelihood opportunities, and for humanitarian actors to deliver aid and services. ltbrgtOver the project duration, UNMAS staff will oversee, train and monitor the teams of implementing partners (IPs) and collect and analyze data through the information management system for mine action (IMSMA). An UNMAS non-technical survey (NTS) team will conduct desk assessments, analysis of historical records, a wide range of other information congregation and analysis functions, and physical visits to communities to collect information from community members. The NTS team will also gather information on EO incidents, victims, survivors and main needs in terms of assistance to facilitate referral and future interventions. A multitasking team (MTT) will conduct technical survey, marking, and EO disposal (EOD) spot tasks. They will also maintain community liaison to keep the concerned communities aware of the EO risks. By assessing the absence/presence of EO contamination in areas where humanitarian actors conduct operations, UNMAS will contribute to the safe delivery of aid and services, and reduce the impact of EO on the civilian population and the humanitarian sector. ltbrgtUNMAS EORE teams will train facilitators from other humanitarian and early recovery actors to deliver EORE to communities and provide EO awareness and focal points training to humanitarian workers to support their safety and ensure integration of EORE messages in their activities. ltbrgtUNMAS will recruit survivors of EO incidents as EORE facilitators who have been trained through another resource of fund during 2023 and are ready to be recruited under this project. These survivors, most of whom have lost one or both limbs to an EO incident, will work with the UNMAS team to deliver EORE to communities. The initiative was extremely successful in 2023 and had a high impact on the communities reached in delivering a powerful message on the EO risks. ltbrgtThe NTS MTT activities in addition to EORE sessions planned under this project will be implemented in Rural Damascus and Aleppo Governorates.lt/pgt
